# Background - DELETE THIS

For this assignment, you are tasked with determining which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) on the West Coast of the US are best suited to developing marine aquaculture for several species of oysters and a species of your choice. Suitable locations will be determined based on range of suitable sea surface temperature (SST) and depth values for the species.

To make your workflow generalizable, you must create a function that has the following characteristics:

    arguments:
        minimum and maximum sea surface temperature
        minimum and maximum depth
        species name
    outputs:
        map of EEZ regions colored by amount of suitable area
        species name should be included in the map’s title

Tip: Building a generalizable workflow

    Remember, functions can be hard to debug! So it’s highly recommended that you build the workflow for a single species (not in a function). Then you can start translating your workflow into a function by identifying the pieces that need to be generalized.

    Questions to ask yourself: which variables can stay the same for each species and which ones would need to change?

# Prepare data

To start, we need to load all necessary data and make sure it has the coordinate reference system.

    - shapefile for the West Coast EEZ
    - bathymetry raster
    - SST rasters
        - combine SST rasters into a raster stack

    Tip
    Make sure to check that these datasets have the same coordinate reference systems! If not, transform them to match.

```{r}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(terra)
library(knitr)
#library(ggpubr)

# Set warnings to display as they occur
options(warn = 1)

# Set ggplot theme
set_theme(theme_bw())

# Set here path
here::set_here("/Users/smsoriano/Documents/Documents - Nawiliwili/UCSB_MEDS/eds223/Aquaculture_Potential_Analysis")
```

```{r}
# LOAD DATA

# Load west coast EEZ vector file
eez <- sf::st_read(here("data","wc_regions_clean.shp")) #|> 
        # Correct invalid geometries to avoid error in st_join when using CRS 4326
        #st_make_valid()

# Load bathymetry raster
bath <- rast(here("data","depth.tif"))

# Load sea surface temp (sst) rasters
sst_08 <- rast(here("data","average_annual_sst_2008.tif"))
sst_09 <- rast(here("data","average_annual_sst_2009.tif"))
sst_10 <- rast(here("data","average_annual_sst_2010.tif"))
sst_11 <- rast(here("data","average_annual_sst_2011.tif"))
sst_12 <- rast(here("data","average_annual_sst_2012.tif"))

# Stack sst rasters
sst_stack <- c(sst_08,sst_09,sst_10,sst_11,sst_12)

# Check resolution and extent of sst_stack
cat("=== Sea Surface Temp Stack (K) ===\n")
cat("Resolution:", res(sst_stack), "\n")
cat("Extent:    "); print(ext(sst_stack))

# Check resolution and extent of bath
cat("=== Bathymetry (m) ===\n")
cat("Resolution:", res(bath), "\n")
cat("Extent:    "); print(ext(bath))
```

```{r}
# Warning - CRS - confirm all three crs match, otherwise stop
if (same.crs(eez,bath) & same.crs(sst_stack, eez)){
    # All three CRS match - true
    print("SST Stack, West Coast EEZ, and Bathymetry data CRS all match!")
} else {
    # CRS match - false
    stop("CRS do NOT match!")
}
```


```{r}
# # Confirm same CRS before proceeding
# cat("Check CRS Match:\n")
# cat("West Coast EEZ vs bathymetry: ", same.crs(eez, bath), "\n")
# cat("SST Stack vs West Coast EEZ: ", same.crs(sst_stack, eez), "\n")

# All CRS match, but EPSG code is missing from sst_stack.
# Assign ESPG:4326 code to sst_stack
crs(sst_stack) <- "EPSG:4326"
```

# Process data

Next, we need to process the SST and depth data so that they can be combined. In this case the SST and depth data have slightly different resolutions, extents, and positions.

    - find the mean SST from 2008-2012 (e.g. create single raster of average SST)

```{r}
# Create raster with 1-layer of mean SST degC from 5-layer raster
sst_mean <- app(sst_stack, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
names(sst_mean) <- "Mean_SST"

# Check input and output raster layers to confirm
cat("Original SST stacked raster has:",nlyr(sst_stack),"layers","\n")
cat("New SST Mean raster has:",nlyr(sst_mean),"layer","\n")
```

    - convert average SST from Kelvin to Celsius
        - hint: subtract by 273.15

```{r}
# Check units of SST_mean raster
minmax(sst_mean)

# Convert SST_mean K to C (local operation - each cell)
sst_mean_C <- sst_mean - 273.15

# Confirm units of SST_mean_C raster
minmax(sst_mean_C)
```

    - crop depth raster to match the extent of the SST raster

```{r}
# Crop the bath raster to the extent of the sst_mean_C raster
# Note: CRS must match
bath_crop <- crop(bath, sst_mean_C)
```

    - note: the resolutions of the SST and depth data do not match
        - resample the depth data to match the resolution of the SST data using the bilinear method approach

```{r}
# Resample bath to match sst_mean_C using bilinear approach
bath_resampled <- resample(bath_crop, sst_mean_C, method = "bilinear")
```

    - check that the depth and SST match in resolution, extent, and coordinate reference system
        - hint: can the rasters be stacked?

```{r}
# Warning - confirm bathymetry and SST raster match before proceeding
# Note: compare crs, resolution, and extent
print("Checking that sst_mean_C and bath_resampled rasters match in CRS, resolution, and extent...")
if (same.crs(bath_resampled,sst_mean_C)){
    # CRS match - true
    print("CRS do match!")
    if (all(res(sst_mean_C) == res(bath_resampled))){
        # Resolution match - true
        print("Resolutions do match!")
        if (ext(sst_mean_C) == ext(bath_resampled)) {
            # Extent match - true
            print("Extents do match!")
            print("Success - sst_mean_C and bath_resampled match in all required raster characteristics.")
        } else {
            # Extent match - false
            stop("Extents do NOT match!")
        }
    } else {
        # Resolution match - false
        stop("Resolutions do NOT match!")
    }
} else {
    # CRS match - false
    stop("CRS do NOT match!")
}
```

```{r}
# Stack sst_mean_C and bath_resampled rasters
ocean_raster <- c(sst_mean_C,bath_resampled)
# Confirm stack
cat("New ocean_raster has",nlyr(ocean_raster),"layers.\n")
cat("Layers are:",names(ocean_raster)[nlyr(ocean_raster)-1],",",names(ocean_raster)[nlyr(ocean_raster)])
```

# Find suitable locations

To find suitable locations for marine aquaculture, we’ll need to find locations that are suitable in terms of both SST and depth.

    - reclassify SST and depth data into locations that are suitable for oysters
        - sea surface temperature: 11-30°C
        - depth: 0-70 meters below sea level
        - hint: set suitable values to 1 and unsuitable values to 0
    - find locations that satisfy both SST and depth conditions
    Tip: finding suitable locations
        The SST and depth rasters should now identify the suitability of locations as 0 or 1. To find locations that have both suitable temperature and depth, you can use map algebra. One idea is to multiply the values of the cells, using the lapp() function.

```{r}
# Set matrix for classify categories - tempC
rcl_matrix_tempC <- matrix(c(
   11,  30,  1
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Reclassify tempC layer and turn resulting categories into factors 
oyster_tempC_zones <- as.factor(classify(ocean_raster[[1]], rcl = rcl_matrix_tempC, others = 0))

# Define level names
levels(oyster_tempC_zones) <- data.frame(
  value = 0:1,
  label = c("Unsuitable", "Suitable")
)

# Set matrix for classify categories - depthm
rcl_matrix_depthm <- matrix(c(
   -70,  0,  1
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Reclassify depthm layer and turn resulting categories into factors 
oyster_depthm_zones <- as.factor(classify(ocean_raster[[2]], rcl = rcl_matrix_depthm, others = 0))

# Define level names
levels(oyster_depthm_zones) <- data.frame(
  value = 0:1,
  label = c("Unsuitable", "Suitable")
)

# Multiply layers to classify by both tempC and depthm
# Note: Only 1*1 cells will stay 1
habitat_class <- oyster_tempC_zones * oyster_depthm_zones

# Rename label
names(habitat_class) <- "Suitable_Habitat"
```

# Determine the most suitable EEZ

We want to determine the total suitable area within each EEZ in order to rank zones by priority. To do so, we need to find the total area of suitable locations within each EEZ.

    - select suitable cells within West Coast EEZs
    - find area of grid cells
    - find the total suitable area within each EEZ
        - hint: it might be helpful to rasterize the EEZ data

```{r}
# Turn eez vector data into raster
eez_raster <- rasterize(eez, habitat_class, field = "rgn")

# Confirm rasterization of eez matches habitat_class raster
# Warning - confirm eez_raster and SST raster match before proceeding
# Note: compare crs, resolution, and extent
print("Checking that habitat_class and eez_raster rasters match in CRS, resolution, and extent...")
if (same.crs(habitat_class,eez_raster)){
    # CRS match - true
    print("CRS do match!")
    if (all(res(habitat_class) == res(eez_raster))){
        # Resolution match - true
        print("Resolutions do match!")
        if (ext(habitat_class) == ext(eez_raster)) {
            # Extent match - true
            print("Extents do match!")
            print("Success - habitat_class and eez_raster match in all required raster characteristics.")
        } else {
            # Extent match - false
            stop("Extents do NOT match!")
        }
    } else {
        # Resolution match - false
        stop("Resolutions do NOT match!")
    }
} else {
    # CRS match - false
    stop("CRS do NOT match!")
}
```

```{r}
# Grid cell area needs to be determined since crs is EPSG:4326 (units = deg)
# Note: m^2 is default unit
habclass_cellarea <- cellSize(habitat_class, unit = "km")

# Multiply each cell in habitat_class by the cellSize areas
# Note: Because unsuitable = 0, unsuitable cells area will = 0
# Note: Only suitable cells (1) will keep the size value (m^2)
habitat_class_area <- habitat_class * habclass_cellarea

# Rename to add units
names(habitat_class_area) <- "Suitable_Habitat_km2"
```

```{r}
# Calculate sum of suitable area in each EEZ using zonal operation
# habitat_class_area = raster where every suitable pixel represents size in m^2
# eez_raster = raster version of EEZ vector (EEZ regions)
eez_priority <- zonal(habitat_class_area, eez_raster, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)

# Sort eez regions by descending area
eez_priority <- eez_priority |> 
    arrange(desc(Suitable_Habitat_km2))
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

# GENERATE FIGURE

# Set color palette
color_palette <- c("gray85", "#0077b6")

# Add back EEZ geometries for plotting
eez_mapv <- eez |> 
    left_join(eez_priority, by = "rgn")


# Create EEZ region map colored by amount of suitable area

tm_basemap(server = "Esri.WorldTopoMap") +
tm_shape(eez_mapv) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "Suitable_Habitat_km2",
              fill_alpha = 0.6,
              col = "#36454F",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = color_palette),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Suitable Area (km^2)",
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right"))) +
  tm_text(text = "rgn_key",
          size = 0.8,
          col = "#36454F") +
tm_compass(position = c("left","bottom")) +
tm_scalebar(position = c("left","bottom")) +
tm_options(component.autoscale = FALSE) +
tm_title("EEZ Regions with the Most Suitable Area for Oyster Aquaculture",
            size = 1.5,
            frame = TRUE) +
tm_layout(# Specify legend title size
          legend.title.size = 1.0,
          # Specify legend text size
          legend.text.size = 0.8,
          # Set font family
          text.fontfamily = "sans",
          # Set inner margins to give scalebar room
          inner.margins = c(0.1,0.1,0.05,0.05)
          )

```
Figure 1: Map of the US West Coast Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ), colored by amount of suitable area (km^2) for oyster marine aquaculture. Suitable area for oyster aquaculture is defined by areas meeting both the temperature requirement of 11-30 degree C, and the depth requirement of 0 to 70 m.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Total suitable area (km^2) for oyster marine aquaculture in each US West Coast Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). Suitable area for oyster aquaculture is defined by areas meeting both the temperature requirement of 11-30 degree C, and the depth requirement of 0 to 70 m."

# Make table using kable
eez_mapv |> 
    select(rgn, rgn_key, Suitable_Habitat_km2) |> 
    st_drop_geometry() |> 
    knitr::kable(col.names = c("EEZ Region", "Region Key", "Total Suitable Habitat (km^2)"))
```
